newsitem.title: UK: UK housing starts fall 12 percent 3 mths to June.
newsitem.headline: UK housing starts fall 12 percent 3 mths to June.

text.p: British housing starts fell a seasonally adjusted 12 percent in the three months to June while total completions were up two percent, the Department of the Environment, Transport and the Regions said.
Private enterprise starts were down 13 per cent while completions were up four per cent.

Housing Association starts of new dwellings in the three months April to June were unchanged compared with the previous three months, but completions fell back. Both starts and completions by local authorities and government departments remained at a low level.

In June alone, 16,600 dwellings were started compared with 14,800 in June 1996. Completions also numbered 16,600 compared with 14,200 in the previous year. Unadjusted figures for the latest three months show 50,200 dwellings were started, up 10 per cent on the same three months a year ago, while completions were up six percent at 45,100.
